meta.purpose: Track the PM OS skill value-eval pass: does invoking each skill produce a materially better result than the base model (Sonnet 5) would produce on the same request with no skill and no extra prompting? The automated judge verdict (auto_verdict_v1/v2) is informational only and has shown run-to-run instability (test cases + baselines are regenerated each run) — it is NOT the decision of record. The 'decision' field is the only authoritative status, and is only ever set by the user, not inferred from the auto-verdict.
known_limitations: Single binary-judge pass per skill; test cases and baselines are regenerated fresh on each run, so verdicts are not directly comparable run-to-run.
Before trusting an auto_verdict for a skill not yet reviewed by the user, check evidence_quality: strong-consistent (agreed across v1 and v2) vs thin-flipped (verdict changed between runs).

auto_verdict_v2.rationale: The skill version adds concrete contingency handling absent from the baseline — a stall fallback ("if you had to decide right now, which way do you lean?") and an explicit rule that any deferral must be named with a date rather than left open — plus a shareable, time-boxed agenda (including a step to loop in Marcus if it's a handoff) that the user can send Priya directly, whereas the baseline stops at talking-point advice with no artifact or plan for what happens if Priya doesn't give a clear answer.
